craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of abiding; vyabhicāri peace (śama) at change standing still in self. Sanskrit-first: svātantryāt (BY-OWN-POWER — kept; discerning's instrument named); sthiti (STANDING — kept; standing IS the doctrine); viśrānti (REST — kept). Rows: 1 (‘standing as his nature’ closes), 9 (makings/unmakings — same words as v6: terminological consistency kept), 12 (śānta-settle: rest…standing). Close: ‘standing as his nature’. Rupture: comma after ‘power’ (discerning turns to resting). Rejected: ‘dwell’ — killed: rest kept; ‘are his essence’ — killed: standing-as-nature kept standing; ‘the autonomous one’ — killed: ‘the free one’ kept (house word). Read aloud: SO of the FREE-one, dis-CERN-ing BY his OWN-pow-ER … MAK-ings AND-un-MAK-ings REST in his OWN-self, STAND-ing AS his NA-ture.

lines: So of the free one, discerning by his own power,
makings and unmakings rest in his own self, standing as his nature.
l4.sanskrit_cite: evam asya svatantrasya nijaśaktyupabhedinaḥ | svātmagāḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārāḥ svarūpatvena saṃsthitāḥ

reads_against.argmap: Where do makings and unmakings stand? → Thus-therefore: self-abiding change, stood not made.
c1_essence: Change self-abides: stood as nature, arrived without departing.
